experiment.steer: S015 §19 no dense rematerialization; §77 the metric that counts; §73 gated claims

kernel.note: the native matvec and the GPU packer are byte-identical to the previous block; only the CPU-side verifier changed

the_lever_was_named_by_the_previous_rece.quoted: verify 60.97% > pack 12.23% > read 7.39% > gpu 6.47%. THE DOMINANT PHASE IS NOW accept_pack ... the next lever is making the HONEST gate cheap, NOT weakening it back toward the cheap dishonest one
the_lever_was_named_by_the_previous_rece.baseline_reproduced: the dense-gate arm here measures verify at 61.595% of wall, against 60.97% recorded in the previous block on a different day and a different process -- the baseline is reproducible

where_the_cost_actually_was.method: profiled accept_pack phase by phase on a real 768x2048 expert BEFORE changing anything
where_the_cost_actually_was.finding: THE GATE'S COST WAS A DENSE REMATERIALIZATION. 84% of the honest predicate was dequantize() building the full dense f32 tensor so it could be multiplied -- the exact `compact bytes -> reconstruct dense -> conventional GEMM` shape S015 §19 rules out, sitting INSIDE the gate that certifies the compact path. The two float64 matvecs it was blamed on cost 0.037 ms each, 1.4% of the total.
where_the_cost_actually_was.why_that_matters: the fix is not a cheaper CHECK, it is the removal of work the verifier should never have been doing. Nothing was traded away.

the_transformation.identity: decoded[r,c] = (q[r,c] - BOUND) * scale[r, c//GROUP], so the group scale factors out of the inner sum and ref[r] = SUM_g scale[r,g] * SUM_{c in g} (q[r,c] - BOUND) * x[c]
the_transformation.second_fold: the -BOUND term collapses to BOUND * SUM_{c in g} x[c], which does not depend on the row at all and is computed once per group instead of rows times
the_transformation.nibbles: contracted where they lie, two per byte, against the even and odd halves of x -- the interleave the dense path materialised is never undone
the_transformation.exactness: float64 accumulation throughout; agrees with the dense path to 8.3e-17 relative, which is machine epsilon and not a tolerance

the_exact_option_was_also_the_fastest.finding: casting the nibbles to float64 first materialises 24 MB of temporaries. Letting einsum promote uint8 against a float64 operand is BIT-IDENTICAL and 1.47x cheaper -- and it also beats the float32 inner product, which is NOT exact. THERE WAS NOTHING TO TRADE: the option that changes no number is also the fastest one measured. The float32 variant is recorded with its price so the choice is visible rather than silently foreclosed.

first_run_of_this_AB_used_the_slower_exa.note: measured, then superseded by the uint8-promotion form before the receipt was written; reported so the 52.3% below is not read as a single leap

prediction_written_before_the_run.note: FIRST RUN of this A/B used an explicit float64 cast of the nibbles and measured +36.34% at 567,093 WU/h -- OUTSIDE its own [12,30] band on the HIGH side, an under-prediction recorded rather than rebased. Letting einsum promote from uint8 is BIT-IDENTICAL and 1.47x cheaper again (1.07 vs 1.58 ms), so this run re-predicts off the measured 0.4175 s wall.

prediction_verdict.the_pattern_is_the_finding: THREE CONSECUTIVE PREDICTIONS IN THIS PIPELINE HAVE COME IN ABOVE THEIR BAND. Tier 1 predicted an 18-25% GPU share and measured 30.88%; the GPU packer predicted 215-270k WU/h and measured 411k; this predicted 570-630k and measured 634k. The bias has ONE mechanism and it is measured below: every prediction held the untouched phases FIXED, and they are not fixed.

cross_phase_interference.claim: removing the verifier's dense temporaries made phases it does not touch faster
cross_phase_interference.read_is_the_clean_one: read_s runs IDENTICAL CODE in both arms and is 1.156x faster in the cheap arm with COMPLETE SEPARATION and both spreads inside the 10% gate (4.5% and 5.9%). pack_s moves the same way, 1.114x with separation, but both arms sit above the gate (14.8%, 10.8%) so it is directional only.
cross_phase_interference.the_control_that_makes_it_credible: gpu_s is FLAT at 1.004x and is the ONLY phase that does NOT separate. If this were a global 'the cheap arm ran in a better minute' artifact the GPU dispatch would have moved with everything else. It did not.
cross_phase_interference.mechanism: the dense path allocated and touched roughly 30 MB of float64 temporaries PER TENSOR -- a 6 MB dense f32 tensor, its 12.6 MB float64 copy, a 12.6 MB float64 copy of the true tensor -- against a 64-tensor loop whose read and pack phases are host-memory-bound. The verifier was evicting the working set of the phases either side of it.
cross_phase_interference.size: 0.0124 s of the 0.190 s saved = 6.5%. Small, real, and enough to put a phase-additive prediction outside its own band.

what_is_left_inside_the_gate.next_lever: verify is still the largest phase at 43.28% and ref_matvec is 74.3% of it. The honest options are (a) move ref_matvec to the GPU, which requires an implementation INDEPENDENT of the native matvec kernel or gate 1 becomes vacuous -- the DEQUANT+DENSE pair P7 already uses as its control is the obvious candidate and shares the nibble convention, which is the exact thing to think about before shipping it -- and (b) the 24.1% spent casting the true tensor to float64, which a float32 matvec would remove at a ~1e-7 relative change.

claim_boundary.what_this_is: a CLEAN gate result, unlike the block before it: both arms inside the 10% IQR gate (dense 9.15%, cheap 7.60%), complete separation (min cheap 607,943 > max dense 423,900), margin 52.3% against worst-arm noise 9.15% = 5.7x.
claim_boundary.reps: 6 alternating pairs, warmed twice on both paths, lake fill SIGSTOPped. Still 6 samples per arm, not the 200 reps this program's own stability audit says a RELIABILITY VERDICT needs; the verdict is admitted on separation as much as on the gate.
claim_boundary.what_it_does_not_show: nothing about the kernels changed -- the native matvec and the GPU packer are byte-identical to the previous block, so no Metal claim moves. This is a CPU-side verifier change measured through a GPU pipeline. Bit-exactness of a pack and a faithful gate still say NOTHING about whether ws_rtn_q4_g64 is adequate for a MODEL; local adequacy does not compose.
claim_boundary.the_thing_that_would_falsify_the_headlin: if the cheap gate accepted anything the dense one rejected. 96 accept_pack calls on real tensors, 32 of them negative controls, ZERO verdict mismatches and worst numeric disagreement 4.3e-16.

headline: THE GATE GOT 2.15x CHEAPER BY DOING LESS OF WHAT IT SHOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN DOING. 84% of the honest predicate was a DENSE REMATERIALIZATION inside the verifier -- §19's forbidden shape, in the one place nobody had looked for it. Contracting the packed nibbles where they lie is 2.15x faster on the phase and +52.3% on WorkUnits/hour, at 4.3e-16 disagreement and zero verdict changes.

bench.machine: Apple M3 Ultra, 60 GPU cores, 96 GiB (receipts/headless/MACHINE_GENOME.json)
bench.rule: S032 §3 -- if quiescence is unknown the state is UNKNOWN, not quiet
bench.provenance: this receipt was written before quiescence was a benchmark input and recorded none. UNKNOWN is what it measured under, not a claim that the machine was busy
